message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a Monopoly trade offer.

I'm p4 with $553 and several unmortgaged properties. The offer is for Kentucky and Indiana Avenue for $200 plus Mediterranean Avenue. This is the same trade I rejected earlier when they counter-offered $300.

Rejecting the offer is correct. The $200 cash lets p2 survive a hit I might collect. Mediterranean Avenue is my emergency mortgage and a brown chip I must never give p3. I will not sweeten the deal.

Mortgaged reds require interest and unmortgage costs. $353 cash cannot survive the next roll's hotel hits.

Unmortgage costs for both reds total $242. They remain useless without Illinois.

p3 is the real threat with light-blue hotels, green four-houses, and all railroads. p2 has a pink monopoly with two to three houses. The reds are dead paper without Illinois, which p3 will never give up.

I considered what to counter with instead. p2's pink monopoly and two get-out-of-jail cards are not useful to me. I own the orange set except for St Charles, which p2 holds.

I own the full orange monopoly but St James and Tennessee are mortgaged. Unmortgaging both costs $198, which I previously rejected to preserve cash cover. I also own both dark blue properties, though Boardwalk is mortgaged.

Boardwalk unmortgage costs $220. I will not pay that either.

Mediterranean is a small asset to keep as a mortgage buffer and to block p3 from completing the brown monopoly. p3 already holds Baltic, so p2 cannot monopolize brown. Still, p2 might trade Mediterranean to p3 later.

I will reject the trade outright. I will not counter, as that would signal weakness or reopen negotiation. The public message should be firm but concise.
